name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset, a knowledge base, an ongoing effort to connect structured image concepts to language. It contains over 108K images where each image has an average of 35 objects, 26 attributes, and 21 pairwise relationships between objects. The dataset includes 5.4 Million Region Descriptions, 1.7 Million Visual Question Answers, 3.8 Million Object Instances, 2.8 Million Attributes, and 2.3 Million Relationships. Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question answer pairs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei

rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Workers were asked to draw bounding boxes and write descriptions for regions, extract objects from descriptions, add attributes to objects, connect pairs of objects with relationships, and write question-answer pairs about images. Each HIT was designed such that workers manage to earn anywhere between $6-$8 per hour if they work continuously. Visual Genome HITs achieved a 94.1% retention rate.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The Visual Genome dataset consists of all 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO's 328,000 images and YFCC's 100 million images. These images are real-world, non-iconic images that were uploaded onto Flickr by users.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All Visual Genome data go through a verification stage as soon as they are annotated. Verification is conducted using two separate strategies: majority voting and rapid judgments. All components of the dataset except objects are verified using majority voting, which involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct. An annotation is added to the dataset if at least two out of the three workers verify that it is correct. Rapid judgments are used only to speed up the verification of objects in the dataset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For region descriptions, workers lowercase, lemmatize, and strip excess whitespace from all descriptions. BLEU score thresholds are used to ensure that new descriptions are dissimilar to previously written descriptions. For objects, attributes, and relationships, similar preprocessing is applied including lowercasing, lemmatization, and stripping excess whitespace. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs are canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools to extract noun phrases and map them to their most frequent matching synset in WordNet according to WordNet lexeme counts, refined by hand-crafted mapping rules for the 30 most common failure cases.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers on Amazon Mechanical Turk were asked to: (1) draw three bounding boxes and write three descriptions for regions in each image, with subsequent workers adding more descriptions until 50 region descriptions were collected per image; (2) extract all objects from each description and ground each object as a bounding box in the image; (3) add attributes to objects or connect pairs of objects with relationships based on the text of the description; (4) write question-answer pairs about images, including both freeform QAs (8 pairs per image) and region-based QAs (around 20 pairs per image). Workers were explicitly encouraged to write descriptions that have not been written before. Bounding boxes must satisfy coverage (covering all objects mentioned) and quality (as tight as possible around the object). All annotations go through a verification stage using majority voting (three unique workers voting on correctness, with at least two required to verify) or rapid judgments (for objects only).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting involves three unique workers looking at each annotation and voting on whether it is factually correct. An annotation is added to the dataset if at least two (a majority) out of the three workers verify that it is correct.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image has an average of 42 region descriptions. For verification, 3 workers vote on each annotation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: A total of over 33,000 unique workers contributed to the dataset. 93.02% of workers contributed from the United States. The majority of workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old. The youngest contributor was 18 years old and the oldest was 68 years old. There was a near-balanced split of 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (Stanford CoreNLP natural language processing toolkit) were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs, and Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically to speed up the object extraction process.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of people with various attributes including gender, age, and activities. Annotator demographics were collected including age, gender, and geographic location.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets show that people playing sports are common. The images range from as small as 72 pixels wide to as large as 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels. Visual Genome images cover 972 synsets. The dataset uses images from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M, which may introduce biases from those source datasets. Certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) are overrepresented due to a bias towards these sports in the images.
rai:dataLimitations: The canonicalization mappings to WordNet synsets are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The precision and recall scores for canonicalization are: Objects (88.0% precision, 98.5% recall), Attributes (85.7% precision, 95.9% recall), Relationships (92.9% precision, 88.5% recall). Current models are unable to reason about complex images effectively, as shown by low accuracy in baseline experiments. Relationships are not visually distinct enough for discriminative models to learn effectively, with only 8.74% top-one accuracy for relationship classification. The dataset's long-tail distribution of answers makes question answering challenging.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding. Specific use cases include: dense image captioning, visual question answering, image understanding evaluation, relationship extraction, semantic image retrieval, attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, object detection, image-to-text tasks, and visual reasoning tasks. The dataset enables models to understand interactions and relationships between objects in images, moving beyond simple object recognition to cognitive tasks.
